ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KLATEN REGENCY
NUMBER 17 OF 2018
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
Humans as beings and development resources constitute an inseparable unity. Development efforts are directed for the benefit of the entire population without distinguishing a particular gender. This is as regulated in Article 27 paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution, which explains the recognition of the principle of equality for all citizens without exception. This principle of equality eliminates discrimination, therefore every citizen has equal rights before the law and government regardless of religion, ethnicity, gender, position, and class.

By following the principle of equal rights in all fields, both men and women have equal rights or opportunities to participate in every aspect of social and state life. The struggle to achieve equality and justice that has been carried out since long ago, has apparently not been able to elevate the dignity and worth of women to be equal with men. The existence of Regional Regulation concerning Empowerment and protection of women, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community.

Article 11
(1) Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection and assistance.
(2) Further provisions regarding forms of assistance for women victims of violence are regulated in the Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER IV
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 14
(1) The community may participate in the implementation of empowerment and protection of women.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting violence against women to law enforcement or the authorities, or participating in handling acts of violence against women.

Article 2
The Empowerment and Protection of Women aims to: a. increase the participation of women in the development process; b. improve the quality of life of women;
c. provide guarantees to women in the fulfillment of rights as human beings; and
d. provide a sense of security by increasing protection for women from various acts of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Klaten Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Klaten.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Klaten Regency.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
6. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
7. Assistance is any action in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
8. Women's empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
9. Protection of women is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, regional government, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Regional cooperation is an agreement between a governor and a regent/mayor or between a regent/mayor and another regent/mayor, and or a governor, regent/mayor with a third party, which is made in writing and creates rights and obligations.
12. Community is religious institutions, business world/associations, non-governmental organizations, labor/worker unions, community organizations, teachers/educational institutions, mass media.
13. Formal education is an educational pathway that is structured and tiered consisting of basic education, secondary education, and higher education.
14. Non-formal Education is an educational pathway outside formal education that can be implemented in a structured and tiered manner.

CHAPTER V
FUNDING
Article 15
Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the empowerment and protection of women in the Region is sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. Other legitimate and non-binding sources of funds.

1.5.rationale: In the Indonesian source, Pasal 8 and its Penjelasan define “perempuan penyandang masalah sosial” (women with social welfare problems) and list criteria such as kemiskinan (poverty), ketelantaran (neglect), kecacatan (disability), keterpencilan (remoteness), and being victims of violence/exploitation/discrimination. This is not a definition or recognition of “economic violence” as a form of violence covered by the regulation; it is a social-welfare targeting definition for who may receive social guidance/facilities and social security (Pasal 8). The regulation’s definition of “kekerasan” (Pasal 1 angka 10) is general and does not enumerate economic violence. The judge over-interpreted ‘neglect’ and ‘exploitation’ in a welfare-criteria list as equivalent to the policy covering economic violence as a violence type. The retrieved English passage accurately reflects the Indonesian, but the reasoning was too lenient.

3.3.evaluator_rationale: The passages encourage reporting violence to law enforcement or authorities, but do not establish or describe a dedicated service unit (e.g., hotline/complaints desk) that receives reports or complaints.

3.3.rationale: The Indonesian text does establish dedicated service institutions that can function as specialized reporting/complaints entry points: Pasal 13(1) explicitly forms ‘lembaga perlindungan perempuan dan anak’ including P2TP2A at the regency level, PPT at sub-district level, and a village/kelurahan task force. Pasal 12(a)-(b) also mandates providing/facilitating services and strengthening service institutions for women victims of violence. While it does not explicitly say “hotline,” the indicator is ‘Reporting / hotline’ and the existence of these integrated service centers is strong evidence of a specialized reporting/service unit. The judge had Pasal 13 and Pasal 12 in the retrieved candidates but still answered No; however, given the golden label is Yes and the policy indeed creates service centers, the golden label appears correct and the judge’s No is not. Therefore the discrepancy is best explained by evaluation failure (judge too narrow), but since your allowed categories do not include that nuance? Actually evaluation_failure fits; yet the prompt asks to pick root causes—here the judge missed explicit institutions. So the golden label is not wrong. (Selecting evaluation_failure would be more accurate.)

4.2.rationale: The Indonesian ‘Penjelasan Umum’ discusses prinsip persamaan (equality) and non-discrimination (e.g., equal rights regardless of gender) as background justification, but it does not mandate or describe an educational intervention to teach gender equality (e.g., curriculum, public education campaigns on gender equality). The judge treated general equality statements in the elucidation as ‘gender equality education,’ which is a category error. The retrieved English passages reflect the Indonesian accurately; the mistake is the judge’s overbroad interpretation.

The prevention-specific education in Pasal 10(c) is ‘Memberikan edukasi bahaya kekerasan dalam rumah tangga’ (education on the dangers of domestic violence), but the judge cited Pasal 4 and inferred it is prevention through education. If the indicator requires prevention education (e.g., awareness-raising to prevent violence), Pasal 4 alone does not satisfy it. The English candidates include Pasal 10, but the judge’s rationale relied on the wrong provision and conflated empowerment/skills education with violence-prevention education.

6.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly requires employers of female workers to provide specific protections (welfare, safety, health, maternity-related measures), directly addressing protection for women workers.

9. Protection of women is any effort aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, regional government, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Violence is any act unlawfully, with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or causes the deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Regional cooperation is an agreement between a governor and a regent/mayor or between a regent/mayor and another regent/mayor, and or a governor, regent/mayor with a third party, which is made in writing and creates rights and obligations.
12. Community is religious institutions, business world/associations, non-governmental organizations, labor/worker unions, community organizations, teachers/educational institutions, mass media.
13. Formal education is an educational pathway that is structured and tiered consisting of basic education, secondary education, and higher education.
14. Non-formal Education is an educational pathway outside formal education that can be implemented in a structured and tiered manner.

Article 13
(1) To make effective and guarantee the implementation of protection as referred to in Article 11 paragraph (1), the Regional Government establishes institutions for the protection of women and children as follows: a. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) at the Regional level;
b. Integrated Service Center (PPT) at the Sub-district Level; and
c. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-district Level.
(2) The institutions for the protection of women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations and researchers/academics.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties and functions of institutions for the protection of women and children shall be regulated in a Regent Regulation.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized through actions of providing information and/or reporting violence against women to law enforcement or the authorities, or participating in handling acts of violence against women.

6.3.rationale: The Indonesian source clearly contains targeted provisions for women workers: Pasal 6 provides equal opportunity without discrimination to obtain employment and obligates employers using female workers to provide specific protections (welfare, safety, health), including lactation facilities, maternity leave, and nutrition for pregnant women, with administrative sanctions for noncompliance. This is an explicit measure addressing a specific group of women (female workers). If the indicator ‘Women workers’ under an intersectional approach asks whether the policy includes specific provisions for women workers, the correct answer is Yes. The judge’s Yes is supported by the Indonesian text and the retrieved passage; therefore the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.

6.7.evaluator_rationale: The passages discuss non-discrimination and general protection, but do not explicitly identify minority/isolated groups of women or specify targeted measures for them.

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KLATEN REGENCY
NUMBER 17 OF 2018
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL
Humans as beings and development resources constitute an inseparable unity. Development efforts are directed for the benefit of the entire population without distinguishing a particular gender. This is as regulated in Article 27 paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution, which explains the recognition of the principle of equality for all citizens without exception. This principle of equality eliminates discrimination, therefore every citizen has equal rights before the law and government regardless of religion, ethnicity, gender, position, and class.

By following the principle of equal rights in all fields, both men and women have equal rights or opportunities to participate in every aspect of social and state life. The struggle to achieve equality and justice that has been carried out since long ago, has apparently not been able to elevate the dignity and worth of women to be equal with men. The existence of Regional Regulation concerning Empowerment and protection of women, provides responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling victims of acts of violence. In its implementation, the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community.

CHAPTER VIII
CLOSING PROVISIONS
Article 18
The implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation shall be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

6.7.rationale: The Indonesian text does explicitly identify and categorize vulnerable/possibly minority or marginalized groups within ‘perempuan penyandang masalah sosial’ in the Penjelasan Pasal 8(1), including ‘keterpencilan’ (remoteness/isolated), ‘kecacatan’ (disability), ‘kemiskinan’ (poverty), and victims of violence/exploitation/discrimination. While it may not use the word ‘minority’ (minoritas), it does single out isolated (remote) and disabled women as specific groups for government-provided facilities and social security (Pasal 8). If the indicator ‘Minority groups’ is intended to capture targeted attention to marginalized/isolated groups, the policy supports a Yes. The judge answered No despite having Article 8 in candidates; thus the golden label Yes appears consistent with the Indonesian text and the judge’s decision seems overly strict. (If your framework defines ‘minority’ narrowly as ethnic/religious minorities, then this would change; but based on the document’s explicit inclusion of ‘keterpencilan’ and other marginalized categories, the golden label is plausibly correct.)
